correctness.rationale: The exponential edge priorities imply the exact count-chain transitions with rates lambda XY/N, XZ/N, YZ/N. Finite-time density convergence follows from bounded O(1/N) jumps, O(1/N) quadratic variation and Lipschitz drift. Equality of the two limiting first classes is invariant; integrating du/dv=p u/v+1/2 gives the complete, sign-checked root classification including p=1 and the zero-residual boundary. The terminal graph satisfies Z(T)-X(T)-Y(T)<=U<=X(T)+Y(T)+Z(T); combining fixed-T convergence with u(T)->0 proves terminal convergence and bounded convergence proves the mean. The actual standalone checker passed 104 exact finite graph generator comparisons, algebraic identities and bounded seeded simulations; no finite experiment is claimed to prove the limit.

originality.rationale: Unlike the equal-rate 2004 multispecies equations and the transitive-species rate-matrix study, the present nontransitive three-class rate matrix has unequal class densities and an exact finite dense-graph terminal law. Its positive-rate critical surface, continuously varying exponent and essential endpoint are not implied by the known equal-rate tripartite product case. The 1986 three-species mean-field paper remains an explicitly named inaccessible plausible source; current evidence does not decisively imply this claim, but uniqueness is not certified.

value.rationale: The exact rate-controlled jamming surface separates a zero-vacancy regime from a positive-vacancy regime on a naturally perfect-matchable graph and gives beta(lambda)=2/(2-lambda), an entire continuum of onset exponents, with an infinitely flat endpoint. Heterogeneous priorities create a physically meaningful structural effect, not just another equal-rate parameter substitution. The result is a finite-volume stochastic theorem with terminal passage justified, not merely a mean-field formal solution.
